summary.en: Build lists by transforming and filtering values, then read nested comprehensions in loop order.
summary.bn: মান বদলে ও শর্ত দিয়ে বেছে লিস্ট বানাও, তারপর নেস্টেড কম্প্রিহেনশনের লুপের ক্রম বোঝো।

notes: Python 3.10–3.12 support all comprehension forms used here. Their loop targets do not leak into the enclosing scope, unlike historical Python 2 list comprehensions.

sections.title: Translate the expression into a loop
Transform, select and build nested results
Read repeated for clauses from left to right
Use compact expressions when they read clearly

examples.title: Convert taka to poisha
examples.explanationHtml: Each amount produces one new integer. The result is [1200, 2500, 4000], while the source list remains [12, 25, 40]. The comprehension does not edit taka.

examples.title: Select passes or label every mark
examples.explanationHtml: The final if removes 35 from passes. The if/else before for chooses a label without removing any item. Consequently the labels list still contains four entries.

examples.title: Flatten rows in reading order
examples.explanationHtml: The row loop runs first. Each row then supplies its values; an empty row contributes nothing. Positions 0, 2 and 4 of flat contain 2, 6 and 10.

examples.title: Transpose a rectangular marks table
examples.explanationHtml: For column zero, the inner comprehension collects 70 and 65. Repeating for columns one and two creates three independent column lists. Their totals are 135, 155 and 175.

examples.title: Build rows without sharing them
examples.explanationHtml: A new inner list is constructed for each row. Marking the first row leaves the second row unchanged. The identity check prints False because the row containers are different.

practice.title: Square each reading
practice.statementHtml: Read a space-separated line of integers, possibly empty. Use a comprehension to print their squares in the same order, separated by spaces.
hints: Place multiplication before for; the input order needs no sorting.

practice.title: Positive discounts
practice.statementHtml: Read a line of integer prices from 0 to 10000. Print prices of at least 100 after subtracting 10, in input order. Print a blank line if none qualify.
hints: Filter the original price, then compute its discounted value.

practice.title: Flatten the classroom
practice.statementHtml: Read r from 0 to 8, then r lines of integers. Each row may be empty. Use a nested comprehension to print all values in row order on one space-separated line.
hints: The first for selects a row, and the second for selects a value.

practice.title: Multiplication grid
practice.statementHtml: Read r and c from 0 to 8 on one line. Build a nested list whose cell at zero-based row i and column j is (i+1)*(j+1). Print each row as space-separated integers; zero columns means blank rows.
hints: Make one inner comprehension per row rather than flattening the products.

quiz.prompt: Which numbers remain after the even filter and square transformation?
quiz.explanation: Zero passes the even filter, and the retained values 0, 2 and 4 are squared.
quiz.code: print([n * n for n in range(5) if n % 2 == 0])

quiz.prompt: How many labels does the conditional expression produce?
quiz.explanation: An if/else expression chooses a value for each input; it does not filter inputs.
quiz.code: print(["P" if n >= 40 else "F" for n in [30, 40, 50]])

quiz.prompt: In which order are the nested pairs generated?
quiz.explanation: The leftmost for is the outer loop; y completes its sequence for each x.
quiz.code: print([(x, y) for x in [1, 2] for y in [3, 4]])

quiz.prompt: Where does a filter belong in a basic comprehension?
quiz.explanation: The pattern is [result for item in source if condition].

quiz.prompt: When should a normal loop replace a comprehension?
options: When several branches and side effects make the expression hard to read
quiz.explanation: Comprehensions describe collected values best; multi-step work is clearer in a loop.

quiz.prompt: Does a comprehension loop variable overwrite an outer variable with the same name?
options: No, the loop target has its own comprehension scope
Only when the source is empty
quiz.explanation: Python 3 keeps the comprehension target separate from surrounding names.

quiz.prompt: What does a comprehension over an empty source return?
quiz.explanation: No iteration appends a value, so the resulting container is empty.

quiz.prompt: Which expression creates a two-dimensional table?
options: [x + y for x in range(3) for y in range(2)]
[[x + y for y in range(2)] for x in range(3)]
quiz.explanation: An inner comprehension makes one row; multiple for clauses in one comprehension flatten results.

quiz.prompt: Why avoid [items.append(x) for x in source]?
options: It creates a list of None results only to perform edits
quiz.explanation: Use a for loop for side effects, or build the desired values directly.

quiz.prompt: What must be true for the shown indexed transpose to work?
options: Every row has the expected number of columns
quiz.explanation: Indexing each row at a column fails if a row is too short.

quiz.prompt: How does a list comprehension use memory?
options: It yields only one item and forgets it
It shares every slot with the source
It stores all result items immediately
quiz.explanation: A list comprehension creates the whole list; lazy generators are a different feature.

keyPoints.en: The expression before for determines each result item.
keyPoints.bn: for-এর আগের এক্সপ্রেশন ঠিক করে ফলের প্রতিটি মান কী হবে।

keyPoints.en: A trailing if selects inputs without reordering them.
keyPoints.bn: শেষের if দিয়ে ইনপুট বেছে নেওয়া হয়, তাদের ক্রম বদলায় না।

keyPoints.en: An if/else expression changes values instead of dropping them.
keyPoints.bn: if/else এক্সপ্রেশন মান বদলায়, কোনো ইনপুট বাদ দেয় না।

keyPoints.en: Nested for clauses follow ordinary outer-to-inner loop order.
keyPoints.bn: নেস্টেড for ক্লজ সাধারণ লুপের মতো বাইরেরটি থেকে ভেতরেরটির ক্রমে চলে।

keyPoints.en: Prefer a normal loop when the comprehension hides the steps.
keyPoints.bn: কম্প্রিহেনশনে ধাপ বোঝা কঠিন হলে সাধারণ লুপ ব্যবহার করো।

examQuestions.question: Distinguish a trailing filter from an if/else result expression in a comprehension.
examQuestions.answerHtml: A trailing if rejects input values, so the output may be shorter. An if/else expression chooses a result for every input. For marks [30, 50], filtering passes gives [50], while labelling gives ["retry", "pass"].

examQuestions.question: Trace [x+y for x in [1, 10] for y in [2, 3]].
examQuestions.answerHtml: The result is [3, 4, 12, 13]. For x equal to 1, y visits 2 and 3; only then does x become 10.

examQuestions.question: Use a comprehension to collect positive even integers from values without changing values.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
values = [-2, 0, 3, 4, 8]
selected = [n for n in values if n > 0 and n % 2 == 0]
print(selected)

The new list is [4, 8]; the original five-item list remains available.
